why_separate: These are recorded apart from the gate identity lists on purpose. They are pre-existing, they are not attributable to any release in this batch, and they move the gate's failure COUNT for reasons that have nothing to do with a diff -- so mixing them into a release comparison makes both unreadable.
what_is_demonstrated_and_what_is_not: Freezing the wall clock demonstrates TIME SENSITIVITY: it shows the outcome depends on a real-clock read rather than on the clock the code was handed. It does NOT identify the offending call site. Naming the exact line that reads time.time() instead of its `now_ts` is a SEPARATE finding, and it has not been made.

defects.lane: the mirror lane (sportsassets/workers/mirror_live.py); untouched by this batch
defects.mechanism_demonstrated: the fixtures capture NOW = time.time() when the mirror-lane fakes are IMPORTED (collection); some path under test reads the real clock when the test RUNS. Once that gap exceeds ~250-270 s the pins break.
defects.reproducer_command: cd backend && RN1X_TEST_DSN=... DATABASE_URL=... ADMIN_TOKEN=t PNL_REPRO_DELAY_S=300 python3 -m pytest tests/test_pnl_l34_review_pins.py -q -p no:randomly -p tools.pnl_clock_gap_plugin

measured.delay_270_s: 3 failed (h1, m1, the fast-tick drift pin)
measured.delay_300_s: 5 failed (those, plus m2 and the per-market read)

eliminated: an import-time effect: importing all 536 modules while running ONLY the three suspects gives 3 passed
the prefix's runtime effects alone: the whole 339-file prefix reaches the file at 243 s elapsed with none of them failing
defects.separate_finding_not_yet_made: the exact call site that reads time.time() instead of the tick's now_ts. Candidates are reachable from mirror_live.tick_once; nothing here names one, and no line has been changed.

defects.lane: sportsassets/obs (stream state selection); untouched by this batch
defects.mechanism: the test reads clock.now(), whose `monotonic` field is time.monotonic() -- container uptime -- subtracts one microsecond and asserts the difference is 0.001 ms within 1e-9. A double's ulp doubles at 2**16 = 65,536 s, so past 18.20 h of uptime the difference lands 6.9e-9 away and the assertion cannot be satisfied.
defects.not_a_regression: it fails STANDALONE in the baseline checkout as well as in the release checkouts, and it is in the baseline's own same-day gate set
defects.the_one_line_fix_not_made_here: scale the tolerance to math.ulp(base.monotonic), or build the Instant from a small fixed base instead of the live monotonic clock

consequence_for_reading_gates: On a long-lived machine both defects are present in EVERY run of every commit, so a gate's failure COUNT is not a release signal. Compare sorted failure IDENTITIES between a baseline and a release taken under the same conditions; see research/evidence/gate/GATE_IDENTITY_RECORD.json.
